result.summary: This is the OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentable trace SDK: a TracerProvider whose spans are serialised to OTLP JSON and handed to no-op hook functions that an external eBPF agent can probe. I checked every file for build-time code, init side effects, network use, process execution, encoded payloads and secret access. The only init-time work is reading OTEL_* limit environment variables, and none of the rest is present.

findings.title: eBPF hook points are no-op functions
findings.detail: tracer.start and span.ended are //go:noinline functions that call no-op package variables. They are documented as being 'implemented in eBPF': an external OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation agent attaches uprobes to read span data and supply sampling decisions. This is the module's stated purpose. The Go code itself does nothing with the data.

findings.title: Init-time environment read for span limits
findings.detail: Span limits are read from standard OTEL_* environment variables at package initialisation. This is an ordinary configuration read with no side effects beyond logging invalid values.

capabilities.explanation: No dynamic code loading or execution. The capability comes from reflection and dynamic dispatch: typeStr uses reflect.TypeOf to name error types, json.Marshal walks span structures by reflection, and the package calls interface methods on caller-supplied options and errors. The package-level function variables `start` and `ended` are no-op hooks that eBPF auto-instrumentation attaches uprobes to, as documented.

No code in the package opens sockets or makes requests. The capability is attributed through transitive dependencies (the otel trace/semconv API, slog, fmt/json formatting of interface values), not through any network call here. With no eBPF instrumentation attached, the SDK produces no telemetry at all.

Comes from unsafe.StringData/SliceData/unsafe.String/unsafe.Slice in the compact Value representation, and from reflection-based encoding/json marshalling and unmarshalling. Nothing executes code chosen at run time.

Pure OTLP-JSON data types with marshal/unmarshal methods; there is no network I/O. The capability comes from transitive standard-library paths such as encoding/json and fmt, which dispatch to interface methods.

data_flows.what: OTLP-JSON encoding of finished span data (names, attributes, events, links, status)
data_flows.to: An externally attached eBPF auto-instrumentation probe (uprobe on span.ended), if one is configured; otherwise a no-op

data_flows.what: Warning naming an OTEL_* limit environment variable that held an invalid value
data_flows.to: Process log via slog (stderr by default)
